questions.q: What twist does the summary offer on Jim Rohn's five-people idea?
a: The five authors you read the most
The five friends you spend the most time with
The five mentors you have met in person
The five books you finish in a year
questions.why: The overview twists Jim Rohn's advice: you become like the five authors you read most.

questions.q: What did Craig Newmark do when shyness held him back?
a: He used the internet to connect people through a growing email list
He hired a publicist to raise his profile
He joined a speaking club to practice conversation
He asked a friend to front his new website
questions.why: Lesson 1 follows Craig Newmark from a small email list to the founding of Craigslist.

questions.q: How did Wendy Kopp finally get funding for Teach for America?
a: She recruited thousands of supporters until the press took notice
She won a grant by rewriting her original proposal
She persuaded the skeptical CEO with a second presentation
She raised the money from her Princeton classmates
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes Kopp recruiting over 2,500 people until news coverage brought the money.

questions.q: What did Sara Blakely do after failing her law school entrance test twice?
a: She took a sales job and later started Spanx
She retook the test a third time and passed
She went to work for a law firm as an assistant
She began selling pantyhose for an established brand
questions.why: Lesson 3 explains that Blakely failed the admissions test twice before finding sales.

questions.q: What did Blakely's door-to-door sales work teach her?
a: It hardened her against rejection, which helped her launch Spanx
It taught her how to manufacture hosiery cheaply
It gave her the idea for a mail-order catalog
It connected her with investors for a new brand
questions.why: Lesson 3 credits her sales experience with the resilience she needed to build Spanx.
